purpose: Phase-2 anatomical registry for the Profile-B simulator, with Phase-2.5 evidence-anchored schematic drawing weights. Defines ONLY the five skin layers, their biologically correct ORDERING, evidence-anchored schematic draw weights, per-species weight profiles, the scale-level -> visibility mapping, static scenes, labels, and an illustrative palette. Loaded by the app; the code hardcodes NO biological values.

scientific_integrity.ordering_confidence: CONTEXTUAL_ANATOMY - the top-to-bottom ordering (air -> surface -> stratum corneum -> viable epidermis -> dermis -> subcutis) is textbook consensus (OpenStax A&P 5.1 CC BY; StatPearls NBK537325).
scientific_integrity.proportion_basis: Phase 2.5: draw weights are now EVIDENCE-ANCHORED (were purely ordinal in Phase 2). For each tissue layer with located literature, the default (human) weight = log10(representative thickness in um); this display-compression keeps thin layers legible. Per-species profiles are kept separately; NO cross-source averaging was performed. See docs/profile-b-anatomy-scale-validation.md.
scientific_integrity.weight_basis: draw_weight = log10(representative_um) for evidence-anchored layers (display-compression, NOT a measurement); subcutis is an ILLUSTRATIVE orientation-only weight (thickness genuinely variable); skin_surface is an interface strip (not a measured layer).
scientific_integrity.why_still_not_to_scale: Even with literature values the dynamic range is ~100x (dermis ~2000 um vs SC ~18 um); a true-to-scale cross-section would render the SC sub-pixel. Weights are therefore log-compressed SCHEMATIC values and the UI must keep the 'schematic - not to scale' caption.
scientific_integrity.rule: Never invent measurements; never average conflicting sources; record disagreement; every value has provenance.

model_scope.statement: The anatomy scaffold is a CONTEXTUAL/generic skin cross-section. The Profile-B evidence spans FOUR separate experimental contexts (ex vivo RAT skin permeation; in vitro HaCaT human keratinocytes; in vitro B16BL6 murine melanoma; in vivo C57BL/6 mouse) kept separate per the frozen biological-visualization blueprint. Human per-layer thicknesses are the best-supported in the literature, so the default scaffold uses the HUMAN profile; RAT and MOUSE profiles are provided but flagged INCOMPLETE. No universal average is invented.

palette.note: ILLUSTRATIVE_COLOR only - restrained, muted, flat fills to DISTINGUISH regions. No gradients, no glow, no concentration/activity encoding.

layers.thickness_basis: interface boundary (not a measured layer); illustrative strip weight

mouse.range_um: very thin (few um; not cleanly resolved)

layers.name: Viable Epidermis
layers.draw_weight_basis: log10(56.6 um) - human representative (Sandby-Moller 2003, dorsal forearm)
layers.role: living epidermal layers below the stratum corneum

layers.name: Dermis
layers.draw_weight_basis: log10(2000 um) - human; 2000 = midpoint of the cited 1-3 mm range used as a DISPLAY anchor only (full range recorded; not a measurement)

human.source: consensus (OpenStax; Turkish J Plast Surg 2018); range wide
human.confidence: MEDIUM (wide range; display anchor = range midpoint, flagged)

rat.range_um: substantial (bulk of skin); no clean per-layer um located

mouse.range_um: bulk of the ~540 um total skin

layers.name: Subcutaneous Tissue
layers.draw_weight_basis: ILLUSTRATIVE orientation-only (NOT evidence-derived) - subcutis thickness is genuinely variable (hundreds of um to several mm) and not defined for a generic cross-section; Profile-B evidence does not reach it
layers.role: hypodermis (orientation-only; not reached by Profile-B evidence)

human.range_um: highly variable (site/BMI dependent); not a fixed thickness

weight_profiles.note: Per-species draw-weight profiles. The layer-level draw_weight above equals the human_contextual profile (the default). rat/mouse profiles retain evidence where located and stay ordinal (flagged INCOMPLETE) where per-layer um were not found. No cross-source averaging.

human_contextual.basis: log10(representative_um) for SC/epidermis/dermis; illustrative for surface/subcutis

rat.basis: viable epidermis log10(20 um) anchored (PMC5620574); SC/dermis ORDINAL (no per-layer um located); INCOMPLETE

mouse.basis: total ~540 um known; per-layer um NOT located -> ORDINAL; INCOMPLETE

scale_levels.note: Populates the Phase-1 ScaleSystem (L1..L6). depth_window is a [top,bottom] fraction of the full tissue stack (0=surface top, 1=subcutis bottom). emphasized = layers drawn at full opacity; others dimmed. clip = cross-section exposes all layers at overview. UNCHANGED from Phase 2.

scenes.title: Cross Section
scenes.note: clean cross-sectional cut exposing all layers

labels.note: Anatomical names only (no explanatory text). Placed at band centre; hidden when a band is below the min pixel height. UNCHANGED from Phase 2.

provenance_sources: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 5.1 (CC BY 4.0) - layer ordering + general thickness consensus
Sandby-Moller J, Poulsen T, Wulf HC. Epidermal thickness at different body sites. (PubMed 14690333) - human SC + viable epidermis um by site
Epidermal thickness in healthy humans: systematic review & meta-analysis (ResearchGate 359694655) - human epidermis
Measurement of Epidermis, Dermis, and Total Skin (Turkish J Plast Surg 2018) - human dermis context
Pharmaceutics 2017;9(3):33 / PMC5620574 (CC BY) - rodent viable epidermis ~20 um; species differences
Multiparametric Analysis of the Skin Barrier of C57BL/6J mice (Annex JVSAH) - mouse total skin ~540 um
